decisions.question: Does knowing how the ball arrived (a cross, a through ball, a carry, a ball just won back) make the value of possession more accurate?
decisions.test: A search on 2020-25, then one confirmation on 1,251 matches from 2013-19 set aside and never looked at: the richer chain must predict which possessions end in goals better, with the whole 95% interval of the improvement above zero.
decisions.result: Better in 7 of 7 seasons; error change -0.000086 (95% interval -0.000098 to -0.000074). Predictive skill up 15%: 0.70% of the variation in goals explained, against 0.61%.
decisions.decision: Adopted: the pitch is 4,132 states, each zone split by how the ball arrived.

decisions.question: Would a re-tuned shot model rate chances more accurately?
decisions.test: One confirmation on 2013-19 matches set aside for it: lower error with the whole 95% interval below zero, and no part of the pitch or game worse calibrated.
decisions.result: Error change +0.00045 (95% interval -0.00006 to +0.00095); calibration slipped in 2 places.
decisions.decision: Not adopted: the expected-goals model stays as it was.

decisions.question: Does a replacement win the ball back in proportion to the danger he faces, or a fixed amount per 90 minutes plus a share of the danger?
decisions.test: Predict each player's own matches that the fit had not seen (58,390), and the first season at a new club for 117 players who moved. A new rule had to be more accurate with the whole 95% interval below zero, in at least 4 of 6 seasons, and no worse for the movers.
decisions.result: The fixed amount plus a share was 7.5% more accurate, in 6 of 6 seasons, and 22% more accurate for the movers.
decisions.decision: Adopted: ball-winning is judged against a fixed amount per 90 plus a share of the danger faced.

decisions.question: How much should winning the ball count against attack?
decisions.test: Lineups of the same club, so team quality stays out: a weight is set only if its 95% interval is above zero and its top is at most three times its bottom. Then the same design on ten foreign leagues (registered 14 October 2026): its rule keeps a weight of 1 unless the data pin down another value.
decisions.result: Within clubs (MLS 2020-25): ball-winning 3.88 (95% interval -1.93 to 10.68), attack 1.22 (0.10 to 2.60): not determined. Abroad, with MLS: ball-winning 3.32 (1.81 to 4.83), determined; attack 0.62 (0.28 to 1.01).
decisions.decision: Ball-winning counts at 3.32 and attack at 0.62, the study's two estimates. Its rule set only ball-winning's weight and kept attack at 1; the two were estimated together, so both are used (16 Oct 2026).

decisions.question: How much of a keeper's season of goals prevented is skill?
decisions.test: Predict each keeper's next season of goals prevented per shot, for keepers in MLS and eleven other leagues: the raw season, the season shrunk toward the average, or every past season weighted by age and shrunk. Fitted on 2017-21, tested on 2022-25; a candidate replaces the simpler one only if its error is lower with the whole 95% interval below zero.
decisions.result: Shrinking beat the raw season: -0.00112 (-0.00134 to -0.00090). Adding earlier seasons: +0.00000 (-0.00003 to +0.00003), no better. Refitted on 2017-25, a season counts shots / (shots + 500): about 19% at a typical 114 shots on target.
decisions.decision: Adopted: keepers are ranked and valued by their season's goals prevented shrunk by that share, against an average keeper; each keeper's page also shows the raw season.

decisions.question: Should team strength come from results, from chances (expected goals), or from both?
decisions.test: Each 2021-25 season predicted by a model fitted on the others; an alternative replaces results alone only if its error is lower with the whole 95% interval below zero.
decisions.result: Half results, half chances: -0.0024 (-0.0049 to -0.0001). Chances alone: +0.0009 (-0.0046 to +0.0063).

decisions.question: When the ratings change, do the forecasts follow?
decisions.test: Only if they predict no worse: each 2021-25 season predicted by a model fitted on the others, and the 95% interval's upper end below +0.002 per match.
decisions.result: Replacement measured from real fill-ins: -0.00026 (-0.00073 to +0.00019). The context chain: -0.00033 (-0.00121 to +0.00052).

decisions.question: When is a skill mostly noise?
decisions.test: When its reliability, within the player's position and at his minutes, is under 0.5: how closely one half of a season agrees with the other (2020-25).
decisions.result: Winning the ball reaches 0.5 at 668-1,176 minutes, depending on position; 3 skills never do within a season: penalties won, not being dribbled past and fouls.
decisions.decision: Those rows are hatched on every player page.

decisions.question: Do the new badges hold up?
decisions.test: Four candidates fixed in advance: beating defenders, aerial duels, a centre-back badge on clearances, blocks and aerial duels together, and High Presser for midfielders only. Each had to repeat at least twice as often as chance, with the low end of a 98.75% interval above chance (stricter, because four were tested at once). A fifth, added afterwards for centre backs: ball won against the danger they faced, at a 99% interval (five tests in all).
decisions.result: Beating defenders: 38.3% (lower bound 29.0%) against 12.8% by chance; aerial duels: 27.0% (lower bound 18.0%) against 10.1% by chance; centre-back defending: 12.8% (lower bound 4.5%) against 9.1% by chance; High Presser, midfielders: 15.8% (lower bound 4.2%) against 4.1% by chance. Centre backs, danger-adjusted: 19.5% (lower bound 8.4%) against 10.7% by chance
decisions.decision: Added: Ankle Breaker, Air Marshal; High Presser now covers central and attacking midfielders; neither centre-back badge was added.

decisions.question: Which badges are shown, and who holds them?
decisions.test: A badge is shown only if its holders are at least twice as likely as chance to hold it again the next season, with the low end of the 95% interval still above chance; checked on every update. A player holds a badge built on a skill only if that skill is reliable at his minutes.
decisions.decision: The rest are not shown, and no badge rests on a skill marked as mostly noise.

decisions.question: Can a player's playing style be named?
decisions.test: 21 styles across six positions, fixed in advance. Each had to be reliable within a season (0.60 between halves, stepped up to a season), repeat the next season at least twice as often as chance, and stay with players who change clubs.
decisions.result: 21 of 21 reliable; 19 of 21 repeat; the club-change test had 1 to 7 movers per style, too few to judge.
decisions.decision: The 19 styles that passed both tests are on player pages (the owner's call while the club-change test is redone); a second club-change test, fixed in advance, runs on fresh players after the 2026 season and can take them off.

decisions.question: Can teams be sorted into tactical styles?
decisions.test: 7 loose labels fixed in advance (possession, direct, high press, counter-pressing, counter-attacking, low block, mid block). Each had to hold from one half of a season to the other, and show up in the other half in the chances it should produce.
decisions.result: 2 of 6 tested pass: possession and direct. Pressing high and sitting deep mostly track how good a team is.
decisions.decision: Possession and direct are the two ends of one scale, so team pages show where each club sits on it (owner, 2026-10-15), with where its chances come from and the three seasons it plays most like, instead of labels. Plays-most-like check: a club that keeps its manager is nearer its own previous season than 92% of all others (median).
